title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (reconstructed from this page and the neighbouring ones). W is a complete DVR with uniformizer p, presumably Witt vectors. Put λ_i = p^{p^i}/(p^i)! = γ_{p^i}(p).

The ring A^{(ν)} is a free W-module with basis the monomials Θ_0^{a_0}…Θ_ν^{a_ν}, 0≤a_i≤p−1. Its relations are:
- (Θ_i+λ_i)^p = [(p^{i+1})!/((p^i)!)^p]·(Θ_{i+1}+λ_{i+1}) for i<ν;
- (Θ_ν+λ_ν)^p = 0.

These are exactly the relations satisfied by Θ_i = γ_{p^i}(T) − γ_{p^i}(p), since γ_{p^i}(T)^p = [(p^{i+1})!/((p^i)!)^p]·γ_{p^{i+1}}(T). So A^{(ν)} is the truncated divided-power polynomial algebra W⟨T⟩/(T^{[n]}, n ≥ p^{ν+1}), recentred at T = p. Indeed T^{[k]} for k<p^{ν+1} corresponds, up to units, to products of γ_{p^i}(T)^{a_i} with 0≤a_i≤p−1.

W^{(ν)} = A^{(ν)}/I, where I is the ordinary (not PD) ideal generated by Θ_0 = T − p. So W^{(ν)} is the truncated PD polynomial algebra specialised at T = p, i.e. (truncation of) W⟨T⟩ ⊗_{W[T],T↦p} W. The page studies how badly specialisation fails to be well behaved: the images θ_i of Θ_i survive, but as torsion.

Lemma (pp. 5-6). Σ w_a Θ^a lies in I iff:
(a) w_a ∈ p^iW, where a_i is the first nonzero component of a;
(b) w_0 ∈ p^{c(ν)}W, with c(ν) = ν + p(p^ν − (p^ν−1)/(p−1)).

Sufficiency.
- Induction step for p^iΘ_i ∈ I (finished on this page). Expand (Θ_i+λ_i)^p and multiply by p^i. The terms with α≥1 die modulo I. The constant terms cancel because λ_i^p = [(p^{i+1})!/((p^i)!)^p]·λ_{i+1} holds in W; that is why Grothendieck crossed them out on p.5. What remains is p^i·u·Θ_{i+1} ∈ I with v_p(u) = 1, hence p^{i+1}Θ_{i+1} ∈ I.
- Last relation. Expand (λ_ν+Θ_ν)^p = 0 and multiply by p^ν. This gives p^ν λ_ν^p ∈ I. Its valuation is ν + p·v_p(λ_ν) = ν + p(p^ν − v_p((p^ν)!)) = c(ν), using v_p((p^ν)!) = (p^ν−1)/(p−1).

Necessity. Let I' be the set of elements satisfying (a) and (b). Sufficiency gives I' ⊂ I, and clearly Θ_0 ∈ I'. If I' is an ideal, i.e. a W-submodule stable under multiplication by each Θ_j, then I ⊂ I'. This stability is 'laissée au lecteur', with a '!' in the margin.

Corollary (normal form). Every element of W^{(ν)} is uniquely Σ w_a θ_1^{a_1}…θ_ν^{a_ν}, with:
- w_a in a set of representatives of W/p^i, where i is the first nonzero index of a;
- w_0 in a set of representatives of W/p^{c(ν)} (completed on p.7).

Equivalently, as a W-module, W^{(ν)} ≅ W/p^{c(ν)} ⊕ ⊕_{a≠0} W/p^{i(a)}. In particular each θ_i (i≥1) is nonzero but killed by p^i, so specialising a PD algebra along a non-PD ideal creates large torsion.

The next page generalises this to quotients by (Θ_0,…,Θ_r). Plausible purpose: explicit computation of divided-power envelopes and their base change over W (e.g. at T ↦ p), for the theory of crystals and de Rham cohomology in mixed characteristic.
errors: Necessity is not actually proved. The key step, stability of I' under multiplication by Θ_j, is left to the reader. It is nontrivial: multiplying by Θ_j raises exponents past p−1, and reducing via the defining relations moves coefficients between components with different 'first nonzero index'. The marginal '!' suggests Grothendieck was aware of this.

Wording slip: the text says I' must satisfy 'I' ⊂ I, Θ_0 ∈ I''. Logically the argument needs I' ⊂ I (from sufficiency) together with I' being an ideal containing Θ_0 (giving I ⊂ I'). This is fine, just compressed.
The numerical identities check out, including for p=2: v_p((p^ν)!) = (p^ν−1)/(p−1) and v_p(binom(p^{i+1}, p^i)·…) = 1. c(ν) agrees with the p.5 formula ν + p[p^ν − (p^{ν−1}+…+1)].

ideas.what: Truncated divided-power polynomial algebra over W, with basis monomials in γ_{p^i}(T) of exponent < p and relations γ_{p^i}^p = unit·p·γ_{p^{i+1}}
ideas.modern_name: Structure of the PD polynomial algebra W⟨T⟩ (Frobenius-type generators γ_{p^i})
ideas.where_published: Standard in Berthelot, Cohomologie cristalline (1974), Berthelot–Ogus (1978)

ideas.what: Specialising a PD algebra at T=p along an ordinary (non-PD) ideal yields a W-module with explicit torsion W/p^{c(ν)} ⊕ ⊕ W/p^i, with explicit exponent c(ν) and normal form
ideas.modern_name: Torsion in PD envelopes / failure of PD envelopes to commute with non-flat base change

ideas.what: Membership criterion for the ideal (Θ_0) via p-adic valuations of coefficients according to the first nonzero exponent
ideas.modern_name: Explicit normal form / Gröbner-type description of a quotient of a PD algebra

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but routine explicit calculation in divided-power algebras over W, with a valuation count and a normal form. The phenomenon (torsion from specialising PD algebras) is well known in crystalline theory; nothing here appears to be a missing result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Θ is written upper-case throughout (Θ_i, \dot Θ_i), not θ.
In 'Multiplions par p^ν', the condition 'p^ν Θ_ν^α ∈ I si α ≥ 1' is correct as transcribed; the underbrace under λ_ν reads p^{p^ν}/p^ν!.
Struck-out text before 'comme c'est un sous-W-module' reads '[-est A.M-]' (likely 'A-module'); the next line begins 'stable par multiplication', consistent with the transcription.
The last displayed condition continues onto the next page ('} w_0 ∈ E_{c(ν)}'), and the indexing 'E_i si a_i est la première coordonnée non nulle' is correct.
